description:
We are building HydroSense-SWOT, an Earth-observation platform using NASA's SWOT radar and GPM data to forecast transboundary flash floods and protect vulnerable agricultural basins.

Our background is in full-stack development and data engineering.
summary:
HydroSense-SWOT is a satellite-data-driven decision-support platform designed to help understand rainfall trends and flash-flood risks in Bangladesh's Haor Basin. Built for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026's “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!” challenge, it combines NASA Earth-observation data with statistical analysis and hydrological modeling.

Its primary module analyzes 25 years (2001–2025) of NASA GPM IMERG Final precipitation data to identify changes in pre-monsoon rainfall patterns. Using PRCPTOT, R50mm, Theil–Sen slope estimation, and autocorrelation-adjusted Mann–Kendall testing, it measures the direction, magnitude, and statistical significance of regional rainfall trends.

A complementary flood-routing module integrates NASA SWOT river observations, GPM IMERG Early precipitation, and Bangladesh Water Development Board river-stage observations to demonstrate how Earth-observation data can support agricultural decision-making.

By connecting long-term climate trends with local flood-risk applications, HydroSense-SWOT aims to help researchers, planners, and agricultural stakeholders better understand environmental change and its potential impacts on vulnerable farming communities.
details:
Project Overview

HydroSense-SWOT is a bilingual, satellite-data-driven environmental intelligence platform developed by Team AUSTrology for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

The platform consists of two complementary modules:

Module 1 — Haor Flood-Routing & Harvest Decision Support

This module demonstrates how satellite observations can support hydrological analysis in the Surma River and northeastern Bangladesh's Haor Basin. Its real-data pipeline is designed to combine NASA SWOT RiverSP river measurements, NASA GPM IMERG Early precipitation estimates, and Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB) river-stage observations. A Muskingum-Cunge routing approach estimates river-stage response under stated hydraulic assumptions. It includes a retrospective 2024 flood-event evaluation and a clearly labelled synthetic demonstration mode. It is not presented as an operational flood-warning system.

Module 2 — Haor Rainfall Trend Explorer

This is the primary response to the challenge. It provides a reproducible workflow for examining 2001–2025 pre-monsoon rainfall patterns using NASA GPM IMERG Final Run V07B daily precipitation data. It derives PRCPTOT and R50mm indicators and applies:

  • Theil–Sen slope estimation to quantify trend magnitude.
  • Modified Mann–Kendall testing (Hamed–Rao method) to account for serial autocorrelation.
  • Analytical 95% confidence intervals and multiple-testing correction.
  • Spatial comparison across three geographic zones.

The analysis is designed to identify where rainfall patterns are changing, how much they are changing, and whether the observed trends are statistically significant.

Technology and Tools

The backend and scientific pipeline use Python, NumPy, SciPy, xarray, NetCDF4, GeoPandas, Shapely, Rasterio, rioxarray, and earthaccess. NASA Earthdata Cloud and GES DISC OPeNDAP support satellite-data acquisition.

The interactive application uses Next.js, React, TypeScript, Recharts, and geospatial visualization tools. The interface supports English and Bengali and is responsive across desktop, tablet, and mobile devices.

Innovation and Impact

The project's main innovation is connecting long-term satellite-derived rainfall trend analysis with a practical hydrological application for a climate-vulnerable agricultural region.

Rather than treating satellite data as isolated visualizations, HydroSense-SWOT demonstrates how Earth-observation measurements, statistical methods, river-network information, and local ground observations can contribute to environmental understanding and agricultural decision support.

The intended beneficiaries include researchers, agricultural extension planners, disaster-management stakeholders, and communities dependent on Boro rice cultivation.

Scientific Transparency

The platform distinguishes authentic satellite observations, observed ground measurements, derived calculations, and synthetic demonstration scenarios. It documents dataset provenance, methodological assumptions, uncertainty, and operational limitations. Historical rainfall trends are not treated as proof of increasing flood frequency or as a prediction of future flood events.
